title: The Grunion Run, xi
logline: Eleventh year. A Newport reader comes to the run because of the strip. Brings the clipping. Wood signs it. First time.

panels.composition: The beach, lanterns, the run. GULLY's coffee line. A READER, a woman in her sixties, holding a folded newspaper, looking for someone. WOOD at the edge with the pad and BARNABY.

image.prompt: a night beach festival with lanterns, a woman in her sixties holding a folded newspaper clipping and searching the crowd, a young man with a drawing pad and a gray-muzzled dog at the edge, muddy watercolor

panels.composition: The reader, having found him, holding out the clipping and a pen.

balloons.text: It's the dog one. From the tides. Would you—

image.prompt: a woman holding out a newspaper clipping and a pen to a startled young man on a night beach

panels.composition: The clipping: the strip, and under it Wood's hand writing, in the margin, exactly what he always writes: A. Finch — Small Wood, OR. And the gull.

image.prompt: close-up of a hand signing a newspaper clipping of a comic strip in the margin with a small gull drawn beside the name
image.notes: He signs it the way he signs the strip. The gull too. Letter after.

panels.composition: Silent. The fish. The lanterns. The reader walking away with the clipping held flat so it won't crease. Wood looking at his own hand.

image.prompt: silent wide night beach panel with silver fish and lanterns, a woman walking away holding a clipping carefully flat, a young man looking at his own hand, a dog, no words

art.palette: limited; Sundays in watercolor, good now
art.paper: bristol; the browser; from 2008 coastal newsprint a week behind

notes: The first signature. He signs it like the margin. The gull.
